prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] Win95-style archery level 1 in a single file at ./game/index.html.

[action] Wrote the whole game in one HTML file: canvas rendering, mouse aim, hold-to-draw power (0.9s full draw), release to shoot with gravity, rising balloons to pop, on-screen score + 30s timer, start panel, win at 15 pops, lose on timeout, WebAudio SFX (draw, shoot, pop, win/lose jingles, last-5s ticks), pixel font from Google Fonts (the only network dependency).

[result] Verified live in the browser: start screen rendered; after START the HUD showed "SCORE 0/15 / TIME 27"; a shot fired and flew (arrow visible mid-air); a second shot hit a balloon — score went to "SCORE 1/15" with a "+1" float and confetti particles. Browser tab closed.

[assumptions] "First level" = one self-contained round (15 pops in 30s), not a level system. Balloons drift down (falling targets) rather than float up, so the archer on the left shoots up-right. Power scales with hold time; no wind.

[evidence] Two gameplay screenshots: HUD + arrow in flight, then score increment + pop particles. No build step; file opens directly.
